questions.q: Identify the two supporting characters who directly enable the protagonist's school enrollment and name the specific action each takes.
questions.a: Correct answer: Mother (ek¡) — she persuades Father and accompanies the narrator to Shri Laksminarayan Muni; Shri Laksminarayan Muni (nÙkk th jko) — he intervenes with the school authorities and guarantees the narrator's admission. A wrong answer that names only Mother misses the institutional gatekeeping role of the teacher; naming only the teacher overlooks the domestic negotiation that precedes institutional access. Both are necessary — one opens the home, the other opens the school.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why Father (nknk) initially opposes the narrator's education, using one piece of textual evidence.
questions.a: Correct answer: Father opposes education because he believes physical labor provides immediate survival ("tUe&Hkj [ksr esa dke djrs jgus ij Hkh gkFk oqQN ugha yxsxk") while schooling offers delayed, uncertain returns. He fears the narrator will become like city clerks who earn little despite degrees. A wrong answer that says "Father hates education" or "Father is cruel" misreads his pragmatic anxiety as malice. The text shows he later accepts the narrator's schooling when persuaded by Shri Laksminarayan Muni — proving his resistance is economic, not ideological.

Reason 1: His equity practices — no corporal punishment, personal attention to weak students ("dkèk loky xyr gks tkrk rks mls os vius ikl cqykdj le>k nsrsA") — create safety the narrator never had.
